hypothesis: A dedicated streaming RCA ingestion and correlation pipeline that (a) normalizes heterogeneous LLM and infra signals into a common event schema, (b) implements explicit correlation keys and temporal windows across requests/sessions/services, and (c) applies controlled sampling and backpressure handling, will: (1) sustain at least 50k LLM interaction events/minute with p95 end-to-end correlation latency under 5 seconds and zero acknowledged-event loss; and (2) produce incident-level correlated contexts with at least 95% of ground-truth-related events attached, when evaluated against a synthetic incident replay benchmark, compared to a baseline batch-oriented pipeline.

baseline.description: Batch-oriented ingestion and ad-hoc correlation pipeline built with periodic file/log ingestion and offline joins.

architecture.ingestion: JSONL event files written locally or to object storage (e.g., ./data/events/*.jsonl) by the synthetic workload generator. A batch job (Python script) runs every N minutes to load new files and append events to a columnar store (e.g., DuckDB or Parquet).
architecture.correlation: Offline correlation step implemented as a separate Python job that executes after each batch load. It performs SQL-like joins across tables (llm_interactions, infra_metrics, traces) keyed on request_id or session_id, plus coarse-grained time windows (e.g., 5-minute buckets).
architecture.event_model: Events from LLM interactions, infra metrics, and traces are stored in separate logical tables with minimal normalization. Correlation relationships are not materialized until the offline job runs.
architecture.throughput_profile: Ingestion throughput is limited by batch job cadence and single-process file parsing. There is no explicit backpressure mechanism: if event generation rate exceeds batch processing capacity, ingestion latency grows unbounded.
architecture.sampling: No adaptive sampling or prioritization; all events from the workload generator are written. If the system falls behind, the design assumes delayed processing, not dropping or downsampling.
architecture.durability: Durability is provided by the file system or object store. Once files are written, the system relies on periodic discovery and processing. A failure between file write and batch job completion leaves files on disk but correlation latency grows.
operational_characteristics: High end-to-end latency due to batch windows and offline correlation.
No explicit backpressure or flow control, so overload manifests as unbounded lag.
Limited utility for near-real-time incident triage because correlated views update only every batch interval.

expected_behavior.throughput_and_latency: Capable of ingesting and correlating up to ~10k LLM interaction events/minute under moderate hardware with batch interval >= 60s, but with p95 correlation latency on the order of the batch interval plus processing time (tens of seconds to minutes).
expected_behavior.correlation_quality: High correlation completeness when the system is not overloaded because all events within the batch windows are available for joining, but reduced temporal precision and difficulty handling late or out-of-order arrivals.
failure_modes: Delayed availability of correlated incident views.
Potential for time-window join errors when clock skew or delayed metrics/traces occur.

treatment.description: Streaming ingestion and correlation pipeline with explicit RCA event schema, keyed correlation across sources, adaptive sampling, and backpressure-aware processing.

architecture.ingestion: Events from the synthetic LLM application and infra simulator are pushed into a message broker (e.g., Kafka, Redpanda, or a lightweight in-repo queue abstraction) via an ingestion API (e.g., /ingest HTTP endpoint or direct producer). A streaming consumer normalizes raw events into a unified RCA event schema and writes them to a durable store with low-latency indexing.
architecture.correlation: A streaming correlator subscribes to normalized events and maintains in-memory and/or state-store-backed correlation state keyed by request_id, session_id, incident_id, and service_name, with tumbling/sliding time windows (e.g., 60–120 seconds) for joining LLM interactions, infra metrics, and traces into incident_context objects.
architecture.event_model: All events conform to a common RCA schema with fields such as: event_id, event_type, ts, source, request_id, session_id, trace_id, span_id, service_name, model_name, prompt_hash, incident_id (synthetic label for replay), severity, and payload. Source-specific details are nested under payload while top-level keys support efficient correlation.
architecture.throughput_profile: Designed to sustain at least 50k LLM interaction events/minute plus associated infra metrics/traces, using partitioned topics/queues and parallel consumers. Backpressure is handled via consumer offsets and bounded internal queues.
architecture.sampling: Implements configurable sampling policies (e.g., keep all events labeled as part of a synthetic incident, probabilistic sampling for healthy traffic) applied at ingestion or normalization. Sampling decisions are recorded in metadata to support accurate interpretation.
architecture.backpressure_handling: When consumer processing throughput falls behind production, the system: (1) exposes lag metrics; (2) can optionally downgrade to coarser-grained correlation (e.g., fewer context joins) under overload; (3) ensures no acknowledged event is dropped by relying on broker durability.
architecture.durability: The broker and the normalized-event store provide durability. Every event written and acknowledged by the broker is processed at-least-once by the correlator. Idempotent writes (e.g., using event_id) avoid duplication in the correlated context store.
operational_characteristics: Near-real-time correlation with target p95 latency < 5s from event ingestion to availability of correlated context for active incidents.
Explicit visibility into lag, throughput, and correlation success rates.
Graceful degradation under load via backpressure and sampling, while preserving high-fidelity views for incident traffic.

expected_improvements_over_baseline.throughput_and_latency: Sustain >= 50k LLM interaction events/minute with p95 end-to-end correlation latency < 5s, compared to tens of seconds to minutes in the baseline.
expected_improvements_over_baseline.correlation_quality: Achieve >= 95% coverage of ground-truth incident-related events in the correlated context for synthetic incidents, despite partial data and sampling, versus lower and more variable coverage in the baseline when load spikes or windows misalign.
expected_improvements_over_baseline.operational_resilience: Maintain bounded lag and controllable degradation modes instead of unbounded backlog growth, with explicit observability into ingestion and correlation performance.

workloads.name: W1-steady-state-mixed-traffic
workloads.description: A steady-state workload generating a mix of healthy and incident-tagged LLM traffic along with corresponding infra metrics and traces.

llm_rps.notes: Results in ~1,800 LLM requests/minute (~54k over 30 minutes); each LLM request may emit 1–3 RCA events (request, response, evaluator signals).

incident_mix.labeling: Synthetic incident generator assigns incident_id and incident_type on affected requests and generates correlated infra anomalies (e.g., elevated latency metrics) and trace spans.

traffic_profile.infra_metrics_frequency: Per-service metrics emitted every 10s per service instance, including latency, error rate, CPU, memory.
traffic_profile.traces: OpenTelemetry-style spans for each LLM request across gateway, orchestrator, model backend, and vector store.

workloads.purpose: Measure steady-state throughput, latency, and correlation completeness under realistic mixed traffic without extreme bursts.

workloads.name: W2-burst-traffic-with-incident-spike
workloads.description: A bursty workload with sudden spikes in LLM traffic and incident occurrence, designed to test backpressure handling and sampling behavior.

traffic_profile.infra_metrics_frequency: Per-service metrics emitted every 5s per instance to accentuate correlation load during bursts.
traffic_profile.traces: Full traces for all incident-related requests; optional sampling (e.g., 20%) for non-incident traffic.

workloads.purpose: Stress-test ingestion, correlation, backpressure, and sampling policies while ensuring that incident-related correlation remains accurate and timely.

workloads.name: W3-synthetic-incident-replay-benchmark
workloads.description: Deterministic replay of a curated set of historical or pre-recorded synthetic incidents for evaluation, using data shipped in the repo.

traffic_profile.source: Static event traces stored under repo path (e.g., benchmarks/synthetic_incidents/*.jsonl) including known incidents (hallucination_spike, routing_misconfig, retriever_outage).

replay_mode.description: Events are replayed with original inter-event delays to reproduce realistic temporal characteristics.
replay_mode.alternative: For speed, an option to compress time (e.g., 10x faster) while preserving event ordering.

traffic_profile.labeling: Each event is labeled with ground-truth incident_id, incident_type, and is_incident_related boolean for evaluation.
traffic_profile.infra_metrics_and_traces: Bundled metrics and trace events correlated by request_id, session_id, and timestamps.

workloads.purpose: Provide a common benchmark across baseline and treatment for measuring correlation completeness, latency, and accuracy against ground truth.

configuration_controls: Use the same hardware profile (CPU, memory, disk type) and OS/container base image for both baseline and treatment runs.
Pin dependency versions (Python, libraries, broker, database) via requirements files and/or lock files committed to the repo.
Use identical synthetic workload seeds (random seeds) and trajectories for baseline and treatment within each workload scenario.
Disable non-essential background processes and rate-limit external network access to reduce noise in latency measurements.

experimental_design.pairing: For each workload (W1–W3), run the baseline and treatment back-to-back on the same environment, then repeat in swapped order (treatment then baseline) to control for warm-cache effects.
experimental_design.randomization: Randomize the order of (baseline, treatment) pairs for each repetition of a given workload to reduce systemic bias.
experimental_design.warmup_and_cooldown: Discard metrics from an initial warmup window (e.g., first 2 minutes) and final cooldown window (e.g., last 2 minutes) where pipeline components are not in steady state.

data_controls: Ensure that synthetic workload generators preserve the same event distribution and labeling between baseline and treatment, differing only in ingestion/correlation architecture.
Use fixed incident definitions and ground-truth labels stored as part of the replay datasets; do not mutate or regenerate labels for different runs.

metrics.name: ingested_events_total
metrics.description: Total number of RCA events successfully ingested by the pipeline during a run (per workload), broken down by event_type (llm_interaction, infra_metric, trace_span, evaluator_signal, etc.).

metrics.name: ingestion_throughput
metrics.description: Average and peak sustained rate at which events are processed from input source (files for baseline, broker for treatment) into the normalized event store.

metrics.name: correlation_latency_p50
metrics.description: Median time from when an event is first produced by the workload generator (generator_ts) to when it is incorporated into a correlated incident_context record (context_ts) accessible to RCA consumers.

metrics.name: correlation_latency_p95
metrics.description: 95th percentile of end-to-end correlation latency, same definition as correlation_latency_p50, across all incident-related events.

metrics.name: correlation_latency_p99
metrics.description: 99th percentile of end-to-end correlation latency, to capture tail behavior under bursts.

metrics.name: correlated_context_completeness
metrics.description: For each incident_id, the fraction of ground-truth incident-related events that appear in the final correlated context objects produced by the pipeline; aggregated as mean and 5th/95th percentiles across incidents.

metrics.name: false_correlation_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of events attached to a given incident_context that are not labeled as is_incident_related in ground truth (per incident_id), aggregated as mean and percentiles; measures over-correlation/noise.

metrics.name: ingestion_lag_p95
metrics.description: 95th percentile delay between event production (generator_ts) and arrival at the ingestion layer (e.g., broker timestamp or file write completion) to control for source-side bottlenecks.

metrics.name: pipeline_backlog_max
metrics.description: Maximum number of unprocessed events in the ingestion/correlation pipeline (e.g., broker lag or internal queue length) during the run.

metrics.name: event_loss_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of events produced by the workload generator that never appear in either the normalized event store or correlation outputs; computed using generator-side sequence IDs.

metrics.name: cpu_utilization_mean
metrics.description: Mean CPU utilization of the primary ingestion and correlation processes for baseline and treatment, as a proxy for resource efficiency.

metrics.name: memory_utilization_peak
metrics.description: Peak resident memory consumption of the ingestion and correlation processes.

metrics.name: sampling_rate_effective
metrics.description: Effective fraction of non-incident events dropped or downsampled by the sampling policy, to contextualize correlation metrics under load.

metrics.name: incident_context_availability_time
metrics.description: Time from the first event of an incident (min generator_ts for events with incident_id) to the time when a usable incident_context summary is first materialized and queryable.

primary.description: Throughput and latency: Treatment sustains target event rate with low correlation latency.
criteria: For W1 and W2, treatment ingestion_throughput >= 50,000 events_per_minute for at least one 5-minute window without event_loss_rate > 0.

For all workloads (W1–W3), treatment correlation_latency_p95 <= 5 seconds for incident-related events, after warmup, while baseline correlation_latency_p95 is expected to be significantly higher (e.g., > 30 seconds for batch-based design).

primary.description: Correlation completeness and accuracy: Treatment maintains high coverage of incident-related events without excessive noise.
criteria: For W3 (synthetic replay), treatment correlated_context_completeness >= 0.95 (95%) averaged across all incident_ids.
For W3, treatment false_correlation_rate <= 0.05 (5%) averaged across incident_ids.

Treatment correlated_context_completeness is statistically significantly higher than baseline for W2 and W3 (e.g., non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals or pre-specified non-parametric test) under high-load phases.

secondary.description: Operational resilience and efficiency under burst load.
criteria: For W2, treatment pipeline_backlog_max is bounded such that correlation_latency_p95 remains below 2x its steady-state value observed in W1.
For W2, treatment event_loss_rate == 0 for incident-related events, even if non-incident events are sampled.

Treatment cpu_utilization_mean and memory_utilization_peak are within acceptable operational limits for the reference hardware (exact thresholds to be defined per environment, but should not exceed 80% CPU and 75% of allocated memory during steady state).

interpretation_notes: If treatment meets throughput/latency targets but correlated_context_completeness falls below 95%, sampling, window sizes, and correlation logic must be tuned and the experiment rerun.
If baseline unexpectedly meets or exceeds treatment on any primary metric, implementation issues or configuration differences must be investigated before drawing conclusions.

failure_modes.name: Event_loss_due_to_misconfigured_offsets
failure_modes.description: Events produced to the broker are not fully consumed by the streaming correlator due to incorrect offset management or consumer group resets.
failure_modes.detection: event_loss_rate > 0 with no corresponding errors in ingest/correlator logs; discrepancy between generator total events and normalized store count.
failure_modes.mitigation: Enable idempotent writes keyed by event_id, verify exactly-once/at-least-once semantics in tests, and add monitoring on consumer group lag.

failure_modes.name: Correlation_state_bloat
failure_modes.description: The correlator retains state for expired sessions or windows, causing memory growth and degraded performance.
failure_modes.detection: memory_utilization_peak grows monotonically over the run; correlation_latency_p95 increases with time even under constant load.
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement explicit TTLs on correlation state (per request_id/session_id/incident_id) and periodic compaction; verify via unit tests and targeted micro-benchmarks.

failure_modes.name: Misaligned_time_sources
failure_modes.description: Clock skew between the workload generator, infra metrics, traces, and ingestion pipeline leads to incorrect correlation windows.
failure_modes.detection: High false_correlation_rate and/or low correlated_context_completeness despite zero event_loss_rate; inspection of event timestamps shows significant skew.
failure_modes.mitigation: Normalize timestamps at ingestion using a single authoritative clock where possible; encode generator_ts vs received_ts fields and adjust correlation windows accordingly.

failure_modes.name: Unbounded_backlog_under_burst
failure_modes.description: During W2 bursts, ingestion exceeds processing capacity and backlog grows without bound, violating latency targets.
failure_modes.detection: pipeline_backlog_max exceeds a pre-defined safe threshold and continues to grow; correlation_latency_p99 spikes and does not recover after the burst.
failure_modes.mitigation: Tune consumer parallelism, broker partitions, and apply more aggressive sampling on non-incident traffic; introduce admission control for optional signals (evaluator scores, verbose traces).

failure_modes.name: Sampling_bias_impacting_RCA_usefulness
failure_modes.description: Sampling policies reduce ingestion volume but inadvertently drop events critical to reconstruct incidents, lowering correlated_context_completeness.
failure_modes.detection: High sampling_rate_effective coincides with low correlated_context_completeness specifically for incidents that span multiple services or longer durations.
failure_modes.mitigation: Adjust sampling policies to always retain full context for incident-tagged traffic (by incident_id or severity) and maintain minimum sampling rates for rare-but-important event types.

failure_modes.name: Baseline_over-optimization
failure_modes.description: Baseline implementation is tuned with features (e.g., mini-batches with short windows) that make it effectively streaming, confounding the comparison.
failure_modes.detection: Baseline correlation_latency_p95 is similar to or better than treatment, and batch interval is very small (e.g., < 5 seconds).
failure_modes.mitigation: Explicitly document constraints on baseline (e.g., batch every >= 60 seconds, no streaming queue) in code and configuration; treat any deviation as out-of-scope for this experiment.

hardware.cpu: At least 8 vCPUs (or equivalent physical cores) per experiment runner.
hardware.storage: 100 GB SSD or NVMe with throughput >= 200 MB/s and low latency.
hardware.network: If using a distributed broker/database, intra-cluster bandwidth >= 1 Gbps; latency < 2 ms within cluster.

software.os: Linux (e.g., Ubuntu 22.04) or equivalent container base image.
software.python: Python 3.10+ with dependencies pinned via requirements.txt or poetry.lock in the repo.
software.broker: Kafka/Redpanda or an in-repo pluggable message queue implementation; baseline may operate without a broker (file-based).
software.database_or_store: DuckDB, PostgreSQL, or another supported store defined in the repo for normalized and correlated event storage.
software.observability: Optional: Prometheus/Grafana stack or lightweight metrics exporter for collecting system-level metrics; otherwise internal logging to JSON files.

configuration.seeds: Use fixed random seeds for workload generators; store them in a config file (e.g., config/seeds.yaml).
configuration.run_profiles: Provide separate YAML/JSON configs for W1, W2, and W3, each specifying RPS, duration, incident mix, and replay mode.
configuration.resource_limits: Optionally use container-level CPU/memory limits to enforce repeatable resource constraints across runs.

run_instructions: Clone the repository and install dependencies:
Start required infrastructure components (if not using in-process mocks), e.g., via Docker Compose:
Verify connectivity to broker and database using provided health-check script:
Generate or validate synthetic incident benchmark data (if not already present):
Run the baseline pipeline for each workload:
Repeat baseline runs for the desired number of repetitions (e.g., 3), randomizing run order as described in controls. Use distinct output directories per run.
Run the treatment (streaming) pipeline for each workload:
Ensure warmup and cooldown windows are configured (either via flags or config) so that reported metrics exclude non-steady-state periods.
After each run, compute experiment metrics by invoking the analysis script, which compares generator logs, normalized events, and correlated outputs:
Aggregate metrics across repetitions and workloads to produce summary tables and plots:

Inspect aggregated metrics to evaluate success_criteria. Document any deviations, suspected causes (e.g., misconfiguration, environment constraints), and rerun experiments if necessary after adjustments.

run_metadata.run_id: string (unique identifier for a single pipeline + workload execution, e.g., 'baseline_w1_run1')
run_metadata.config_files: list of strings (paths to workload and pipeline configs used)

environment_summary.hardware: JSON object summarizing CPU, memory, storage type, and any container limits
environment_summary.software: JSON object summarizing OS, Python version, broker/database versions

schema.generator_ts: float or ISO 8601 (event creation time at generator)
schema.incident_id: string or null (ground-truth incident for synthetic runs)

schema.received_ts: float or ISO 8601 (time at ingestion layer)
schema.normalized_ts: float or ISO 8601 (time after normalization, if different)
schema.incident_id_hint: string or null (if pipeline infers or propagates incident association)

schema.context_id: string (unique ID per correlated context, often matching incident_id for synthetic incidents)
schema.incident_id: string or null (pipeline-inferred ID or ground-truth for replay)
schema.created_ts: float or ISO 8601 (time when context first materialized)
schema.updated_ts: float or ISO 8601 (time of last update during the run)
schema.event_ids: array of strings (all events attached to this context)
schema.summary: JSON object (optional) with derived aggregates or LLM-generated summaries

schema.summary_by_workload_and_pipeline: object keyed by [workload_name][pipeline_type] with aggregates such as mean, std, and confidence intervals for each metric
schema.comparison_stats: object summarizing baseline vs treatment deltas and significance tests for key metrics (correlation_latency_p95, correlated_context_completeness, false_correlation_rate, event_loss_rate)

logs_and_traces.pipeline_logs: Paths to structured logs for ingestion and correlator processes (e.g., results/.../logs/*.log.json).
logs_and_traces.infra_metrics: Optional Prometheus or other metrics snapshots exported during runs for deeper hardware/resource analysis.
